chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from someone else from our companions, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the apostate: he is asked to repent. So if he repents (fine), or else he is killed. And the woman, when she reneges from Islam, is asked to repent. So if she repents and returns (fine), or else she is kept imprisoned for ever, and her imprisonment is constricted upon her.

key_terms.خُلِّدَتْ فِي السِّجْنِ: She is kept imprisoned for ever/indefinitely

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment between a male and female apostate in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational Shia distinction in the penalty for apostasy (ridda), where males face execution after a three-day period of repentance, while females are confined to indefinite imprisonment (habs) without death. This ruling, primarily attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reflects the juristic view that the female apostate's punishment is corrective confinement rather than capital execution, distinguishing it from the male ruling. The text highlights the procedural emphasis on 'istitab' (seeking repentance) for both genders before the final penalty is applied.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from someone else from our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the apostate: ‘He would be asked to repent. So if he repents (fine), or else he would be killed, and the wife, when she reneges from Al-Islam, would (also) be asked to repent. So if she repents and returns (fine), or else she would be imprisoned for ever, and her imprisonment would be constricted upon her’.
